title: Graded soft-failover policy with probationary variant promotion for region-tier routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current fallback triggers are binary and global: when a region or tier crosses a hard threshold (429s, error rate, timeouts) we immediately cut traffic or switch to a fallback variant. This causes sharp user-visible regressions and churn during transient load spikes or when a single tenant causes elevated signals.

Goal: Implement a graded 'soft-failover' system that promotes a fallback model variant in a probationary mode with progressively stricter gating, per-region and per-tenant probation windows, and hysteresis. The system should combine multiple signals (429 percentile, p95/p99 tail latency, model-level error/token-failure rate) into a probabilistic promotion score and only escalate to full circuit-breaker trips after sustained degradation.

How this fits Redwood: Improves reliability and user experience for hosted and dedicated deployments by avoiding abrupt cutovers, reducing false positives from transient spikes, and providing extensible hooks for routing policies (tier-based, regional, and per-tenant). This also enables smoother private deployments where strict SLAs require measured failover behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Router supports a 'probationary' traffic split: 90% primary / 10% fallback for N minutes under first-tier trigger
Promotion score calculator merges signals (429-rate, p99 latency, token error-rate) and produces a normalized 0..100 score
Policy supports three escalation phases: probationary, staged-promotion, full-cutover, each with configurable durations and decay windows
Per-tenant and per-region state tracked with decaying counters so noisy tenants do not permanently poison routing decisions
Dashboard with SLO heatmap and per-policy timeline is available in Console for real-time inspection
Automated canary rollout (5% traffic) for the new policy enabled behind a feature flag; rollback on regression within 15 minutes
E2E chaos tests simulate transient 429 spikes and validate that soft-failover keeps tail error growth < 2x versus baseline
Documentation and runbook updated: how to tune thresholds, interpret promotion score, and emergency abort procedure

notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative promotion avoids churn but increases exposure time to degraded primary model; we selected multi-signal scoring to reduce false positives.
Decision: start with 3 signals (429-rate, p99 latency, model token-failure) and add anomaly detectors later if needed.
Follow-up: evaluate adding capacity-aware weighting so high-capacity regions have stricter thresholds.
Fallback variants: prefer smaller/quantized variants first (faster, cheaper) before full model swap to preserve output quality as long as possible.
